presentation.label: AUDIO IN FX
presentation.summary: Two knobs on the FX track's DISTORTION page send the AUDIO IN jacks into the master distortion and compressor, and into the delay and the reverb.
presentation.overview: On stock the AUDIO IN jacks reach the sampler, its monitor and USB, and EXT IN joins after the distortion. Audio In FX plays AUDIO IN through the Rytm's own effects: D (STE) puts it in the analog mix before DIST and COMP, and E (IFX) feeds the delay and the reverb at once. Both at 0, with nothing locked, leave the Rytm as stock.
highlights: Run a synth or a guitar pedal through the master distortion and compressor.
Send AUDIO IN to the delay and the reverb on their own levels.
Two knobs on the stock DISTORTION page: D into the mix before DIST, E (IFX) into the delay and reverb. Real stock parameters, saved with the kit, with FUNC + turn stops at 0, 110 and 127.
Stock's parameter, scene and performance locks on both.
Tap encoder D to sum the input to mono on both paths.
At 0 nothing changes: every audio word stays as stock wrote it.
usage: Plug a source into AUDIO IN L and R. Press FX, then FLTR.
Turn D (STE) up: the source plays through COMP and DIST.
Raise AMT to drive it. AMT distorts the drums too: DIST is one stage.
Turn E (IFX) up to send the source to the delay and the reverb.

access.location: FX track, DISTORTION page (FX, then FLTR): knobs D and E.
steps: Turn D (STE) for the level into DIST and COMP.
Turn E (IFX) to send it to the delay and the reverb.

controls.name: STE / MNO
controls.doc: Knob D, DISTORTION page. AUDIO IN into the analog mix before DIST and COMP. 0 is off, 110 passes the converter's level unchanged, 127 is about 1.33x, +2.5 dB. FUNC + turn jumps 0, 110, 127. A stock parameter: kit-saved, parameter, scene and performance locks.

controls.name: IFX
controls.doc: Knob E, DISTORTION page. AUDIO IN to both the delay and the reverb input, on the same scale. FUNC + turn jumps 0, 110, 127. A stock parameter: kit-saved, parameter, scene and performance locks.

controls.name: Tap of encoder D
controls.doc: DISTORTION page. A short press with no turn adds L and R to mono on both paths, and the knob reads MNO; another tap goes back to stereo. Not saved: it starts stereo. Not with a trig, FUNC or NO held, a pad held in scene or performance mode, nor in running live recording.

limitations: AUDIO IN jacks only. EXT IN is an analog sum after DIST and cannot be rerouted.
DIST is one stage: AMT distorts the input and the drums alike.
Both knobs save with the kit and their locks with the pattern, as stock's own. Mono is not saved.
E feeds the delay and the reverb at one level: the FX track has no third saved word for a separate reverb level.
Mono is L + R: one cable keeps its level, and a loud stereo source can clip digitally. It is not saved.
Level, noise and latency not measured on a unit.
Built for OS 1.74 only, with core-ar2 0.7.

load.display: About 0.65 % of a block for D above 0, 1.3 % for E (two buffers): 2 % with both (static estimate)
load.conditions: Static estimate from the compiled code: about 28 instructions a frame for each knob above 0, at the Rytm guide's 0.023 % of a block per instruction a frame. With all knobs at 0, a few instructions a block. Not measured on a unit.

tests.summary: On the author's Analog Rytm MKII: AC20 and AC21 (this module beside the RC12 and RC14 sets) passed levels, locks, page copy and clear, kit and pattern saves, scene and performance locks and the mono tap; AC21 fixed a tap blocked by a pad that stock's key table read as held. rytm-emu: both knobs at 0 give digital silence and each reaches the output. Level, noise and latency are not measured.
